text:
1. Create a B-tree index on `(customer_id, created_at DESC)` so the filter, order, and `LIMIT 20` are one index range scan.
2. Replace `SELECT *` with the columns you need and add them via `INCLUDE` so the plan can stay index-only.
3. Run `ANALYZE orders` after the index build and confirm with `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` that it stops after 20 rows.
thought:
Preparing three concise one-line suggestions to optimize the slow Postgres query.

The best fix is a composite index on `(customer_id, created_at DESC)`. It covers the filter, sort, and limit in one pass. Also avoid `SELECT *` to reduce I/O.

The third suggestion is to include the needed columns in the index using `INCLUDE` so the query stays index-only.

Run `ANALYZE` on the table so Postgres uses the new index instead of a sequential scan. Verify the plan with `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` to confirm an Index Scan with Limit.
